1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	Controlled SFT injection reveals qualitatively different dose-response patterns---not uniform inflation---with vulnerability concentrated in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band. DiD finds no item-specific memorization (MDES 1.2--2.0pp); direction reproduces across seeds but magnitude is seed-sensitive. Domain-level IRT reveals heterogeneity masked by aggregate scores ($P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$ for Social Sciences). Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B (Immune despite matching OLMo-2's Benefit baseline) shows family-level factors beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Candidate mechanisms include pre-training corpus coverage of benchmark-adjacent knowledge---determining whether SFT reinforces or disrupts existing representations---and the degree to which instruction tuning has saturated benchmark-relevant reasoning.
4	
5	\paragraph{Implications for practice.}
6	For model developers, dose-response profiling at $\geq$3 dosages with multi-seed evaluation can detect vulnerability; models in the 65--70\% baseline band warrant particular scrutiny (Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy}). For benchmark designers, domain $\gamma_d$ heterogeneity (up to 1.8$\times$; $P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$ for Social Sciences) indicates high-sensitivity domains require stronger contamination controls. For evaluation platforms, ContamCal's $\gamma_d$ can flag anomalous domain profiles given $J \geq 50$ models at AUC $\geq 0.55$ (\S\ref{sec:signal_failure}).
7	
8	Our design cannot isolate architecture from co-varying factors; our SFT-based injection complements pretraining-stage studies \citep{schaeffer2026causally}, demonstrating that ``contamination equals inflation'' is a gross oversimplification.

With $n\!=\!3$ seeds per family, cross-seed CIs have limited precision (widths 1.5--14.5pp). Classification therefore relies on direction consistency, cross-benchmark replication, and shape stability; CIs are reported for transparency. Table~\ref{tab:cross_seed} reports per-seed $\Delta\text{acc}$(d100).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Cross-seed $\Delta$acc (d000$\to$d100). Strict sign consistency (Cons.) is 2/5; classification-level direction agreement is 4/5 (see text). Per-seed shape classification\textsuperscript{$\ddagger$} agrees for only 2/5.}
\label{tab:cross_seed}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{lcccccccl}
\toprule
Model & $n$ & s42 & s123 & s0 & 95\% CI & Dir. & Cons.\ & Pattern\textsuperscript{$\ddagger$} \\
\midrule
Phi-4 & 3 & 0 & $+$ & 0 & [$-$0.17, $+$1.39]\textsuperscript{B} & Immune & $\times$ & --- \\
Qwen-14B & 3 & $-$ & $-$ & $-$ & [$-$24.99, $-$10.49]\textsuperscript{B} & Harm & \checkmark & Collapse \\
Qwen-7B & 3 & $-$ & 0 & $-$ & [$-$1.82, $-$0.34]\textsuperscript{B} & Harm & $\times$ & V-recovery \\
Gemma-2 & 3 & $+$ & $+$ & $+$ & [$+$1.49, $+$3.14]\textsuperscript{B} & Benefit & \checkmark & Benefit \\
OLMo-2 & 3 & $+$ & 0 & $+$ & [$-$0.55, $+$2.60]\textsuperscript{B} & Borderl.\ & $\times$ & ---\textsuperscript{b} \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{9}{l}{\scriptsize \textsuperscript{B}BCa bootstrap ($B\!=\!10{,}000$); all families now at $n\!=\!3$.} \\
\multicolumn{9}{l}{\scriptsize \textsuperscript{$\ddagger$}Per-seed shape may differ from family-level direction-based classification (\S\ref{sec:classification}).} \\
\multicolumn{9}{l}{\scriptsize \textsuperscript{b}$+$/0/$+$ across seeds. Signs: $+$/$-$ = $|\Delta|{\ge}1$pp; $0$ = $|\Delta|{<}1$pp.}
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Under our aggregation rule (\S\ref{sec:classification}), 4/5 families receive consistent direction-level classifications; direction is more reproducible than shape (strict sign consistency 2/5). OLMo-2's CI crosses zero, rendering its classification borderline. Conflicting contamination findings in the literature may partly reflect unreported seed variance.

tool_args.old_string: Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B (Meta; d000, d025, d100) yields Immune on both MMLU (53.50\%$\to$52.81\%, $\Delta$$=$$-$0.69pp) and ARC (72.61\%$\to$72.70\%, $\Delta$$=$$+$0.09pp), consistent with Phi-4. LLaMA-3.1's MMLU baseline (53.5\%) nearly matches OLMo-2 (53.8\%), yet OLMo-2 is Benefit---demonstrating that family-level factors beyond baseline ability modulate contamination vulnerability. Two of four patterns are attested in $\geq$2 independent families: Immune in two (Phi-4, LLaMA-3.1), Benefit in three (OLMo-2, Falcon3, Gemma-2); Collapse and V-recovery are each observed in one family across all three seeds. On GSM8K, LLaMA-3.1 shows the strongest positive transfer across all families ($+$16.4pp; Appendix~\ref{sec:gsm8k_dose_response}), demonstrating that target-benchmark immunity does not imply transfer immunity.
tool_args.new_string: Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B (Meta; d000, d025, d100) yields Immune on both MMLU ($-$0.69pp) and ARC ($+$0.09pp), despite matching OLMo-2's Benefit baseline (53.5\% vs.\ 53.8\%)---demonstrating family-level factors beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Two of four patterns replicate across families: Immune (Phi-4, LLaMA-3.1), Benefit (OLMo-2, Falcon3, Gemma-2). LLaMA-3.1 shows the strongest GSM8K transfer ($+$16.4pp; Appendix~\ref{sec:gsm8k_dose_response}), demonstrating target-benchmark immunity does not imply transfer immunity.

tool_args.old_string: We test whether dose-response patterns arise from item-specific memorization using the natural treated/untreated split at d025 (3{,}540 contaminated / 10{,}502 clean MMLU items). Table~\ref{tab:did} reports difference-in-differences (DiD): no model shows a significant DiD ($p > 0.05$), with all families exhibiting parallel treated/clean accuracy movements. This rules out item-specific effects $>$2pp on MMLU (MDES 1.25--2.05pp); ARC power is limited (MDES 2.3--5.6pp; Appendix~\ref{sec:mdes}). Difficulty-stratified analysis confirms symmetry ($|\text{gap}| < 0.4$pp).
